description.value: Canoe Cultures is an Indigenous-led organization in Vancouver dedicated to the art, heritage, and living culture of the canoe, presenting visual art, carving demonstrations, festivals, and guided tours on False Creek. Cultural canoe tours depart from Concord Pacific Community Park and are led by Indigenous guides who share Coast Salish history and traditions. The organization also mounts exhibitions at the Vancouver Maritime Museum and runs school and corporate programs, making it a distinctive cultural stop for cyclists touring the False Creek seawall.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and provides primary evidence. Canoe Cultures is an active Indigenous-led arts organization offering public canoe tours launching from 50 Pacific Boulevard (Concord Pacific Community Park) on False Creek; the contact page confirms phone 778-386-4248. No website content mentions bike parking, washrooms, water refill, or any other cyclist-specific amenities — all such fields default to null. OSM has no tags, phone, or address to cross-check, so contact_confirmed fields reflect what the website supplies independently.
concerns: OSM record has no address, phone, or tags — 50 Pacific Boulevard address is taken from the website's tour launch point, not an organizational office address.
No OSM ID present; record appears to originate from a manual addition rather than an OSM node.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active, publicly accessible Indigenous cultural organization with tours, exhibitions, and festivals operating in Vancouver; directly relevant to cycling tourists on the False Creek seawall.
enrichment_extras.notes: The launch site at Concord Pacific Community Park (50 Pacific Blvd) is adjacent to the False Creek seawall cycling route. Facilities at the park itself (bike racks, washrooms) are under the park's management and not confirmed by Canoe Cultures' website.

wow_evidence: Indigenous-led canoe culture organization: guided canoe tours on False Creek with Coast Salish history, carving demos, exhibitions; Indigenous cultural tour-operator ladder 2/3.
